methodology: Selected, attributed incidents and regional reports affecting Assyrian people or their historically associated Syriac and other Christian communities. Includes historical research and contemporary reported accounts. No independent incident verification is implied. Events may overlap geographically; map shading counts catalogue records, not victims, rates or unique attacks. Markers show approximate representative place coordinates, not incident addresses.

records.title: Massacres of Assyrian communities in Hakkari
records.summary: Assyrian villages in Hakkari were attacked during Bedir Khan Beg's campaign, with killings, enslavement and forced flight recorded in histories of the region. This regional marker does not imply a single incident site.
records.actor: Forces allied to Bedir Khan Beg

records.title: Renewed attacks on the Assyrians of Tiyari
records.summary: A further campaign against Assyrian communities in the Tiyari area followed the violence of 1843. Exact village-level incident boundaries require further archival reconstruction.
records.actor: Forces allied to Bedir Khan Beg

sources.title: Hakkari historical region - referenced history

records.title: Sayfo: destruction of Assyrian communities in Tur Abdin
records.summary: During the First World War, Assyrian and Syriac Christian communities were targeted by mass killing, attacks and forced displacement. This entry covers the wider Tur Abdin region, not a single village or independently quantified death toll.
records.actor: Ottoman authorities and participating local armed forces, as described in historical research

records.summary: Gunmen killed the priest and three deacons after Mass near Holy Spirit Church in Mosul, following threats directed at their ministry.

records.summary: The Chaldean Catholic archbishop was abducted after leaving church; his driver and bodyguards were shot, and his body was found days later. This is catalogued as an attack on the Assyrian-linked Christian community.

sources.title: On Vulnerable Ground - Human Rights Watch

records.summary: Father Adel Youssef, an Assyrian Orthodox priest, was shot and killed in Baghdad's Karrada district.

records.title: Threats and attacks drive Christian families from Mosul
records.summary: UNHCR reported that Christian Iraqis fled Mosul following direct and indirect threats and intimidation, including communities of Assyrian and related church traditions. The figure reported at that time was not independently confirmed by UNHCR.

records.title: Killings of Christians ahead of Iraqi elections
records.summary: Human rights reporting described a series of killings of Christians in Mosul, including a man and his sons, amid claims that intimidation was connected to upcoming elections. The source does not establish each victim's ethnicity.

records.summary: Buses transporting Christian students to the University of Mosul were attacked. Contemporary accounts differed on the number of injured; the catalogue does not reconcile those totals into a single estimate.

records.title: Our Lady of Salvation church massacre
records.summary: Armed militants stormed the Syriac Catholic church during Sunday worship, killing clergy, worshippers and members of the security forces. Published victim totals vary by whether security forces and bystanders are included.
records.actor: islamic state of iraq, affiliated with al-qaeda, according to contemporary reports

records.summary: A coordinated wave of bombings targeted Christian homes, killing residents and injuring others, as documented in an official country-of-origin review.

records.title: daesh ultimatum and expulsion of Mosul's Christians
records.summary: Following the capture of Mosul, daesh demanded that Christians convert, pay a levy or leave. Homes were marked, property was confiscated and families fled, including Assyrians from several church communities.

records.title: Christians flee attacks around Qaraqosh
records.summary: UNHCR reported that up to 10,000 people fled the predominantly Christian Assyrian town of Qaraqosh after mortar fire near the town. This was an earlier displacement wave, distinct from the August occupation.
records.actor: Armed opposition forces in the area

records.title: daesh captures Qaraqosh during Nineveh Plains offensive
records.summary: The August offensive drove much of Qaraqosh's Christian population from their homes and disrupted nearby Assyrian and Syriac towns. Reported regional displacement figures should not be treated as counts for Qaraqosh alone.

records.title: Child reportedly taken during forced departure from Qaraqosh
records.summary: Human Rights Watch recorded the account of a Christian mother who said an armed fighter took her three-year-old daughter during a forced evacuation, corroborated by another witness. This is attributed testimony, not a resolved court finding.

records.summary: USCIRF described a dispute over school curricula in which Kurdish-led authorities reportedly ordered the closure of Assyrian and Armenian schools. School leaders said the required curriculum undermined their distinct identities.

records.summary: A UK Home Office assessment reports continued intimidation and unequal treatment of Christians in Iraq, including at checkpoints and concerning property. This entry summarises a country-wide pattern and must not be read as a single Baghdad incident.
records.actor: Various state and non-state actors cited in the assessment
